facts.text: The little lorikeet is a small green parrot with a red face, found only in Australia.
facts.quote: It is a small parrot, predominantly green in plumage with a red face.

facts.text: Young little lorikeets have a paler orange face and a brown bill and iris, unlike adults.
facts.quote: Immature individuals have a paler orange face and a brown iris and bill.

facts.text: Little lorikeets are sociable birds that often flock with rainbow, musk and purple-crowned lorikeets.
facts.quote: The little lorikeet is gregarious and often flocks with rainbow, musk and purple-crowned lorikeets.

facts.text: They feed mostly on nectar and pollen from woodland trees such as Eucalyptus, Angophora and Melaleuca.
facts.quote: Little lorikeets feed mostly on nectar and pollen of flowers in the open canopy of woodland trees like Eucalyptus, Angophora and Melaleuca species.

facts.text: They sometimes snack on fruit, including native mistletoe and even introduced loquats from orchards.
facts.quote: They have also been known to feed on native grasstrees (Xanthorrhoea spp.), and occasionally on fruit like the native mistletoe and introduced loquat (Eriobotrya japonica). They will occasionally visit orchards.

facts.text: The nest is a tree hollow holding 3-5 matte white eggs, incubated for around three weeks.
facts.quote: The nest is a hollow in a tree and a clutch of 3–5 matte white roundish eggs, measuring 20 x 16 mm, is laid. The incubation period is around three weeks.

facts.text: The little lorikeet has picked up plenty of nicknames, including tiny lorikeet, red-faced lorikeet and gizzie.
facts.quote: Other common names include tiny lorikeet, red-faced lorikeet, gizzie, slit, and formerly a local indigenous term gerryang.

facts.text: Even in Australia, the little lorikeet is uncommon in captivity and has a reputation for being difficult to keep.
facts.quote: Even in its native country, it is uncommon in captivity. It has a reputation of being difficult to keep.

facts.text: The species is listed as Endangered in South Australia and Vulnerable in New South Wales.
facts.quote: The species is currently listed in South Australia as 'Endangered' under the National Parks and Wildlife Act (1972). In NSW the species is listed as 'Vulnerable' under the Biodiversity Conservation Act (2016).
